mohamed.s: Quick Q - Anjali just told me she'll be on extended bereavement and also observing a two-week religious fast that overlaps with our final promotion calibration window. She's concerned about being penalized in this cycle. Any suggestions?

anjali.p: Hi all 12 I'm grateful for the support. I lost a close family member and also have planned religious observance that can't be moved. I want to make sure my contributions are reviewed fairly. Happy to provide documentation for bereavement and let HR know about the observance.

tara.hr: I'm sorry for your loss, Anjali. First, condolences. This is absolutely something we can accommodate. For bereavement we usually accept a short note or HR intake; for religious observance we can make scheduling and timeline adjustments. We'll need to document interim steps so calibration committees have context, while preserving confidentiality.

mohamed.s: Appreciate that. My main concern: calibration deadlines are strict (manager writeups due by Friday). If we extend or defer, will that affect promotion eligibility or bias calibrators? We want fairness but can't keep delaying the whole cycle.

calibration-mgr: From calibrations POV, we have options: 1) allow a manager extension for writeups with a documented reason, 2) allow a deferred eligibility for this cycle (meaning not considered for promotion now but auto-included in next cycle), or 3) accept manager-provided supplemental context and previous period performance data so the committee can deliberate without delays. We prefer #3 to preserve eligibility while protecting timing.

tara.hr: Option 3 is a good compromise. HR can draft confidential context blurb that managers can attach to the packet: short explanation that the employee has a documented accommodation request (bereavement/religious observance) and that supplemental context will be included. This keeps the employee in the cycle and informs calibrators. Important: this note must be limited access.

anjali.p: I would prefer to stay in the cycle if possible. If managers can include previous 6-month work evidence and not rely on real-time interviews or live panel feedback during my absence, that would help. I'm comfortable with HR drafting a confidentiality blurb.

mohamed.s: I can compile the last 6 months of PRs, releases, and impact notes. I'm also happy to offer written answers to any calibration questions rather than live meeting.

tara.hr: Great. Action items: 1) Anjali, please file a short intake note to HR (no need for clinical docs for bereavement; for religious observance a calendar block and optional note is fine). 2) Mohamed, please gather the 6-month evidence and any manager narrative by EOD Thursday. 3) HR will prepare a confidential accommodation blurb and provide guidance to calibrators on limited access. 4) If any live interviews or presentations are part of calibration, we'll accept written alternatives.

people-ops-bot: Case created: HR-8567 - "bereavement + religious observance: calibration accommodations (Anjali P)". Intake timestamp 1855010500. Assigned: tara.hr.

calibration-mgr: We'll accept the manager packet and the HR blurb. Reminder to keep grading rubrics consistent and avoid anchoring bias; we'll allocate one extra reviewer to balance where feasible.

mohamed.s: Thanks. I'll get the packet ready and add the written Q&A option. Mohamad will also note any live-demo alternatives as recorded videos.

anjali.p: Thank you all. I appreciate the option to stay in cycle and the privacy steps. I'll submit the intake after lunch and share my calendar blocks for the observance.

tara.hr: Thank you, Anjali. I'll draft the confidential blurb and post it in this thread for sign-off (manager + employee). We'll also add the 2-week deferral option if you prefer to step out of the cycle, but no pressure. Check-in scheduled in 7 days. :white_check_mark:
